learn: Spanish has two ways to say you. Tú is for friends, family and children. Usted is for adults you respect, like a teacher or a doctor.
¿Cómo estás? uses tú. ¿Cómo está usted? uses usted.
Señor means Mr., señora means Mrs. and señorita means Miss.
check: Which do you use with your teacher?
lessons.try: Greet a grown-up with buenos días, señora or señor, ¿cómo está usted?

learn: Me llamo Leo. Tengo ocho años. Vivo en Nogales. Me gusta el fútbol.
Vivo en means I live in.
Soy alto (tall), soy simpático (friendly), soy divertido (fun).
lessons.try: Write five sentences about yourself in Spanish.

learn: ¿Dónde vives? Vivo en Tucson. ¿Qué te gusta? Me gusta leer.
When you answer a question, use a whole sentence.
Listen carefully to the question word to know what to answer.
lessons.try: Play a question ball game: throw the ball, ask a question, the catcher answers.

learn: Yo soy, tú eres, él or ella es.
lessons.try: Make three "ser" sentences about people you know.

learn: Vivo en Tucson. Vivo en una casa.
Say your city, not your street address.
check: Online you share your ___, not your street.
lessons.try: Tell a partner your city and state.

learn: Endings change for boy or girl.
lessons.try: Match countries to nationality words.

learn: Many people speak more than one language.
lessons.try: Survey the class about languages.

learn: Write: Soy ___. Me gusta ___. Tengo ___ años.
lessons.try: Write and illustrate a self-portrait poem.
Video introduction in Spanish.

learn: Sesenta and setenta sound alike, so listen for the s and the t.
lessons.try: Count by tens to cien and back.

learn: Use y between the tens and ones: sesenta y cuatro (64), ochenta y ocho (88).
Noventa y nueve (99) is the biggest two-digit number.
Read the tens first, then y, then the ones.
lessons.try: Roll two dice to make a number and say it in Spanish.

learn: Más means plus. Menos means minus. Son means equals.
lessons.try: Make up five math problems and read them in Spanish.
Chant tens to cien.
Play big number bingo.
Sort number cards into par and impar.

learn: Mido un metro veinte: I am 1.20 m tall.
check: Most of the world measures in...
lessons.try: Measure your desk in centímetros.
Solve three Spanish word problems.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Numbers to 100
lessons.try: Number bingo final.

learn: ¿Qué hora es? means what time is it?
Es la una means it is one o'clock. Son las dos means it is two o'clock.
Use es la for one o'clock and son las for every other hour.
check: How do you say it is three o'clock?
lessons.try: Look at a clock four times today and say the hour in Spanish.

learn: Y media means half past. Son las cuatro y media is 4:30.
Y cuarto means quarter past. Son las seis y cuarto is 6:15.
Menos cuarto means quarter to. Son las ocho menos cuarto is 7:45.
check: Son las seis y cuarto is...
Son las ocho menos cuarto is...
lessons.try: Draw clocks for 2:30, 5:15 and 9:45 and write the time in Spanish.

learn: A las siete means at seven. A las siete me levanto. At seven I get up.
De la mañana means in the morning. De la tarde means in the afternoon. De la noche means at night.
A las ocho de la noche me acuesto. At eight at night I go to bed.
lessons.try: Write your daily schedule with times in Spanish.

learn: Son las dos, son las tres...
Use es for one, son for the others.
lessons.try: Set a clock and say the time.

check: Son las tres y diez is...
lessons.try: Read ten clock faces aloud.

check: 8:00 in the morning is las ocho de la...
9:00 at night is las nueve de la...
De la tarde means in the...
lessons.try: Make a timeline of your day.

check: Use it to talk about a...
lessons.try: Ask a partner when they eat lunch.

learn: When it's noon in Arizona, it's 8 p.m. in Madrid in winter.
Mediodía is noon; medianoche is midnight.
lessons.try: Compare times in three cities.
Narrate your day with times.

learn: Las matemáticas, las ciencias, la lectura (reading), el arte, la música, la educación física (PE).
Mi clase favorita es el arte means my favorite class is art.
¿Cuál es tu clase favorita? asks what your favorite class is.
lessons.try: Ask three classmates their favorite class.

learn: El cuaderno (notebook), las tijeras (scissors), el pegamento (glue), la regla (ruler), el borrador (eraser).
Los crayones and los marcadores are crayons and markers.
¿Me prestas tus tijeras? means can I borrow your scissors?
lessons.try: Pack a backpack and name each thing in Spanish.

learn: Levanten la mano means raise your hand. Abran los libros means open your books.
No entiendo means I do not understand. ¿Puede repetir, por favor? asks to repeat.
¿Cómo se dice...? means how do you say...?
lessons.try: Use ¿cómo se dice? to ask about three new words.
Tell your favourite subject and why.
Write your school day schedule in Spanish.

check: ¿Cómo se dice...? asks how you ___ something.
¿Puedo ir al baño? asks to go to the...
lessons.try: Use three classroom questions this week.

learn: Escribo (I write), leo (I read), estudio (I study).
Present tense yo forms end in -o.
Tell what you do at school.
lessons.try: Act out school verbs for a partner to guess.

learn: Some schools start in February (southern hemisphere).
check: In Chile, the school year often starts in...
Seasons are ___ in the southern hemisphere.
lessons.try: Compare your school with one in Chile.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: School Day
lessons.try: Tour of our school in Spanish.

learn: Alto is tall and bajo is short. Joven is young and mayor is older.
Tiene el pelo largo means has long hair. Tiene los ojos cafés means has brown eyes.
Es is used for what someone is like.
lessons.try: Describe someone in your family in three sentences.

learn: Mi hermana es graciosa. Adjectives change o to a for girls.
Good friends see the best in each other.
check: A girl who is funny is...
lessons.try: Write three kind adjectives about a friend.

learn: Ask yes or no questions: ¿Es alto? ¿Tiene lentes?
Answer sí, es alto or no, no es alto.
No goes before es to make it negative.
check: Does he or she wear glasses?
Does he or she have a dog?
lessons.try: Play guess who with family photos, asking questions in Spanish.
Describe a cartoon character.
Describe three family members.
Pick three traits that describe you.

learn: Él es alto. Ellos son altos.
check: Ellas son altas means they are...
lessons.try: Describe pairs of people with son.

learn: Frida Kahlo was a painter from Mexico.
Roberto Clemente was a baseball player from Puerto Rico.
lessons.try: Make a poster about one famous person.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Describing People
lessons.try: Guess Who game in Spanish.

learn: Los padres (parents), los hijos (children), el primo and la prima (cousins).
El tío and la tía (uncle, aunt), los abuelos (grandparents), los nietos (grandchildren).
Mi tía es la hermana de mi mamá. My aunt is my mom's sister.
lessons.try: Draw your family tree and label it in Spanish.

learn: De shows belonging. El libro de Ana means Ana's book.
Mi (my), tu (your) and su (his, her or their) also show belonging.
Mis means my for more than one: mis hermanos.
lessons.try: Point to five things and say whose they are using de.

learn: Families gather for birthdays, weddings (bodas) and holidays.
In many Latin American families, a girl's fifteenth birthday is a big party called la quinceañera.
Abrazos (hugs) and besos (kisses) are common greetings in families.
lessons.try: Tell about a family celebration you went to.

learn: Mi hermano, tu prima, su abuelo.
lessons.try: Describe whose things are whose.
Extend your family tree.
Tell three things your family does together.

learn: Many people have two last names.
check: Many Spanish speakers have ___ last names.
The first surname traditionally comes from the...
lessons.try: Write your name the Spanish way.

learn: A celebration of a girl's 15th birthday.
An important tradition in many families.
lessons.try: Draw a quinceañera celebration.
Family tree presentation.

learn: Las verduras are vegetables: la zanahoria (carrot), el tomate, la lechuga, el maíz (corn), la papa (potato).
El aguacate is avocado. El chile is a chili pepper.
Corn, tomatoes, avocados and chiles were first grown in the Americas.
check: Which food was first grown in the Americas?
lessons.try: Name five vegetables you can find in your kitchen.

learn: ¿Cuánto cuesta? means how much does it cost?
Cuesta dos dólares means it costs two dollars. In Mexico, money is the peso.
Es caro means it is expensive. Es barato means it is cheap.
lessons.try: Play market with play money, asking ¿cuánto cuesta?

learn: Buenos días. Quisiera tres manzanas, por favor. Aquí tiene (here you are).
Un kilo is about two pounds. Una docena is a dozen.
Always say gracias to the seller.
lessons.try: Act out buying fruit at a market stall with a partner.

check: Un kilo de tomates is a kilo of...
lessons.try: Weigh fruit on a scale.

learn: Es muy caro: it's very expensive.
lessons.try: Role-play bargaining politely.
Build a pretend market with stall signs.

check: 50 pesos for something costing 30 gives change of...
lessons.try: Practise paying and getting change.

learn: Read a short story about a market.
check: A retell tells the story in...
Find the ___ words in the story.
lessons.try: Retell the story with drawings.
Market role-play final.

learn: El banco (bank), el correo (post office), la panadería (bakery), el supermercado, el restaurante.
La estación de bomberos is the fire station. La iglesia is a church.
El cine is the movie theater.
lessons.try: Draw a small town map and label six places in Spanish.

learn: A la derecha means to the right. A la izquierda means to the left. Derecho or todo recto means straight ahead.
Dobla a la derecha means turn right.
Cerca means near and lejos means far.
lessons.try: Give a partner directions in Spanish to walk across a room.

learn: Voy en carro (by car), en autobús (by bus), en bicicleta (by bike), a pie (on foot).
¿Cómo vas a la escuela? asks how you go to school.
Walking and biking are healthy and good for the air.
lessons.try: Survey your class: ¿cómo vas a la escuela? Make a chart.
Give directions across the classroom.

learn: El parque está cerca de la escuela.
lessons.try: Map your neighbourhood with near and far.

learn: En coche, en autobús, en bicicleta, a pie.
lessons.try: Graph how classmates get to school.

learn: Salida means exit; entrada means entrance.
lessons.try: Make classroom signs in Spanish.

learn: Many towns have a central plaza.
People meet, talk and celebrate there.
A church and city hall are often nearby.
check: A plaza is a town's central...
City hall is often ___ the plaza.
lessons.try: Draw a town plaza.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Around Town
lessons.try: Treasure map with Spanish directions.

learn: El fútbol is soccer. El béisbol, el básquetbol and el tenis sound like English.
Juego al fútbol means I play soccer.
Soccer is the most popular sport in most Spanish-speaking countries.
check: El fútbol in most countries means...
Which sport is most popular in Spanish-speaking countries?
lessons.try: Ask your family which sports they like.

learn: Leer (read), dibujar (draw), cantar (sing), bailar (dance), nadar (swim), cocinar (cook).
Me gusta dibujar means I like to draw.
Words that end in ar, er or ir are action words called verbs.
check: Words ending in ar, er or ir are...
lessons.try: Make a list of your top three hobbies in Spanish.

learn: ¿Te gusta nadar? Sí, me gusta nadar. No, no me gusta nadar.
Me gusta mucho means I like it a lot. No me gusta nada means I do not like it at all.
check: I do not like it at all
lessons.try: Interview someone about four hobbies and record their answers.

learn: Juego al fútbol. Juegas al béisbol.
Use it for games and sports.
check: Juego al fútbol means I play...
lessons.try: Say which sports you and friends play.

learn: Toco la guitarra. Toco el piano.
check: Toco el piano means I play the...
lessons.try: Mime an instrument for others to guess.

learn: Say how often you do hobbies.
lessons.try: Make a "how often" chart.

learn: Many famous athletes come from Spanish-speaking countries.
Baseball is popular in the Caribbean.
check: Baseball is very popular in the...
lessons.try: Research a sport popular in one country.

check: Survey answers can be shown in a...
lessons.try: Survey and graph classmates' hobbies.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Sports and Hobbies
lessons.try: Hobby presentation.

learn: Mexico is just south of Arizona. It has deserts, mountains, jungles and long beaches.
Its capital, Ciudad de México, is one of the biggest cities in the world.
Mexico has 32 states, like Sonora, right next to Arizona.
check: Which Mexican state is next to Arizona?
lessons.try: Find Sonora and Ciudad de México on a map.

learn: Long ago, the Maya and the Aztecs built great cities in Mexico.
The Maya built pyramids and made a calendar and a way of writing.
The Aztec city Tenochtitlan was built on a lake, where Mexico City is today.
lessons.try: Draw a pyramid like the ones the Maya built.

learn: Mariachi bands play violins, trumpets and guitars and wear big sombreros.
Papel picado is colorful paper cut into patterns and hung for celebrations.
Alebrijes are brightly painted fantasy animals carved or made from paper.
lessons.try: Fold and cut tissue paper to make your own papel picado.

learn: Mexico has 32 federal entities: 31 states and Mexico City.
Each state has its own food and traditions.
check: The Mexican state next to Arizona is...
lessons.try: Find Sonora on a map.

learn: Millions of monarchs fly to Michoacán each winter.
They travel from Canada and the US.
check: Monarchs travel from Canada and the...
lessons.try: Map the monarch migration.

learn: Chocolate, corn and chilli came from Mexico.
lessons.try: List foods that came from Mexico.

learn: Papel picado is cut paper banners.
check: Papel picado is made of cut...
lessons.try: Make papel picado.
Make a flag and shout "¡Viva México!"
Mexico fair project.
